name: rename
synopsis: int renameat(int olddirfd, const char *oldpath, int newdirfd, const char *newpath);
int renameat2(int olddirfd, const char *oldpath, int newdirfd, const char *newpath, unsigned int flags);
description: rename() renames a file, moving it between directories if required. Any other hard links to the file are unaffected, and open file descriptors remain valid. If newpath exists, it is atomically replaced.

parameters.name: oldpath
parameters.description: The old pathname of the file or directory to be renamed

parameters.name: newpath
parameters.description: The new pathname for the file or directory

parameters.name: olddirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor for interpreting relative oldpath (for renameat and renameat2)

parameters.name: newdirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor for interpreting relative newpath (for renameat and renameat2)

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to modify behavior, such as RENAME_NOREPLACE or RENAME_WHITEOUT (for renameat2)

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Write or search permission is denied for the directories involved
olddirfd or newdirfd is not a valid file descriptor (for renameat and renameat2)
The file or directory is in use and cannot be renamed
oldpath or newpath points outside accessible address space
Invalid argument, such as attempting to make a directory a subdirectory of itself, or invalid flags
newpath is an existing directory, but oldpath is not
A component of the path does not exist
A path component is not a directory
Operation not permitted, such as due to sticky bit or insufficient privileges
oldpath and newpath are on different filesystems
newpath already exists and RENAME_NOREPLACE is specified (for renameat2)
